title: Workers' Self-Management Law Introduced in Yugoslavia
note: Basic Law passed by Yugoslav Federal Assembly on June 26, 1950. All facts confirmed.

title: Rijeka Integrated into Yugoslavia After Paris Peace Treaty
note: Rijeka ceded to Yugoslavia under 1947 Paris Peace Treaty; event year of 1951 represents administrative consolidation period. Core facts accurate.

title: Forced Agricultural Collectivization Reversed in Yugoslavia
note: KPJ abandoned collectivization by spring 1953. Yugoslavia's uniqueness among socialist states confirmed.

title: London Agreement Resolves Trieste Dispute — Croatia Gains Istria
note: London Memorandum signed October 5, 1954. Zone B (including Croatian Istria) assigned to Yugoslavia. Facts confirmed.

title: First Mass International Tourism Season on the Dalmatian Coast
note: No web sources confirm 1958 specifically as the first mass international tourism season. Tourism development on the Dalmatian coast in the late 1950s is plausible but this specific claim is unverifiable from available sources.

title: Zagreb Film Wins Academy Award — Croatian Animation Acclaimed
note: Surogat directed by Dušan Vukotić won Oscar for Best Animated Short at the 1962 ceremony for films released in 1961. First non-American film to win in that category. Facts confirmed.

title: INA Oil Company Founded — Croatia's Petroleum Sector Organized
note: INA was established on 1 January 1964, not 1962, through merger of Naftaplin with Rijeka and Sisak refineries. Year off by 2.

title: New Yugoslav Constitution Strengthens Republican Autonomy
note: Yugoslav parliament approved new constitution April 7, 1963, renaming the state SFRY and devolving power to republics. Facts confirmed.

title: Major Yugoslav Economic Reforms Liberalize Croatian Enterprises
note: 1965 reform introduced dinar devaluation, enterprise autonomy, and foreign trade liberalization. Gastarbeiter emigration confirmed. Facts accurate.

title: Ranković Removed — Croatian National Movement Gains Space
note: Ranković removed at Brioni Plenum on July 1, 1966, after illegal wiretapping accusations. Political opening for Croatian Spring confirmed.

title: Declaration on the Croatian Literary Language — Landmark Cultural Act
note: Declaration published March 13/17, 1967 in Telegram. Eighteen Croatian institutions signed; Miroslav Krleža among signatories. Political storm and reprisals confirmed.

title: Adriatic Oil Pipeline (JANAF) Construction Begins
note: JANAF construction began in 1984 and became fully operational at end of 1989, not 1970. Year off by 14.

title: Croatian Spring Crushed — Tito Arrests National Movement Leaders
note: Karađorđevo meeting December 3, 1971; Tito forced resignations of Croatian leadership. At least 741 expelled from party, hundreds imprisoned. Stjepan Mesić arrested. Facts confirmed.

title: Franjo Tuđman Imprisoned for Croatian Nationalist Writings
note: Tuđman was sentenced to two years in prison in October 1972 (served ~10 months), not 1973. Year off by 1.

title: New Yugoslav Constitution Grants Croatia Near-State Sovereignty
note: 1974 constitution granted republics near-sovereign status including formal self-determination. Kosovo and Vojvodina near-republican status confirmed.

title: Dubrovnik Designated UNESCO World Heritage Site
note: Dubrovnik designated UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1979, among the first wave of sites. Facts confirmed.

title: Tito Dies — Yugoslavia Enters Uncertain Era Without Its Unifier
note: Tito died May 4, 1980 in Ljubljana at age 87. Rotating collective presidency system confirmed. Facts accurate.

title: Yugoslav Foreign Debt Crisis Hits Croatian Economy
note: Yugoslav foreign debt crisis escalated from 1980 onward causing economic deterioration throughout the decade. Facts plausible and consistent with sources.

title: Serbian Academy Memorandum Published — Croatian Alarm at Serbian Nationalism
note: SANU Memorandum draft leaked to Večernje novosti on September 24, 1986. Milošević's simultaneous rise confirmed. Croatian alarm response confirmed.

title: Yugoslav Hyperinflation Reaches 250% — Croatian Economy Destabilized
note: Sources indicate Yugoslav inflation averaged 75% in the 1980s up to 1988, with severe hyperinflation exploding only in late 1989 and peaking 1992–1994. 250% specifically for 1988 is not confirmed; actual 1988 rate was substantially lower.

title: Croatian Democratic Union Founded by Franjo Tuđman
note: HDZ founded June 17, 1989 by Franjo Tuđman and Croatian dissidents. Mass rallies and path to independence confirmed.

title: First Free Elections — HDZ Wins Landslide, Tuđman Becomes President
note: First free elections April–May 1990, HDZ won decisively. Tuđman elected president May 30, 1990. New constitution adopted December 22, 1990. Facts confirmed.

title: Serb Rebellion in Krajina — Log Revolution Begins Armed Conflict
note: Log Revolution (road blockades by Croatian Serbs) is confirmed as opening act of armed conflict, backed by JNA and Serbian state. Facts accurate.

title: Croatia Declares Independence — June 25, 1991
note: Independence declared June 25, 1991 simultaneously with Slovenia; Brioni moratorium confirmed; all ties severed October 8, 1991. Facts accurate.

title: Battle of Vukovar — City Destroyed After 87-Day Siege
note: 87-day siege confirmed; city fell November 18, 1991. Thousands killed or detained, mass graves found nearby. Facts accurate.

title: Dubrovnik Bombarded — UNESCO World Heritage Site Under Siege
note: JNA and Montenegrin forces shelled Dubrovnik in 1991. Prosecuted as war crime at ICTY. Facts confirmed.

title: International Recognition — Germany Leads, UN Membership Secured
note: Germany recognized January 15, 1992; Croatia admitted to UN May 22, 1992 (178th member). UNPROFOR deployment confirmed. Facts accurate.

title: War Refugee Crisis — 500,000 Croatians Internally Displaced
note: Large-scale internal displacement from Serb-controlled territories confirmed. 500,000 figure consistent with sources on the Croatian War of Independence.

title: Croatian War Economy — GDP Falls 40% from 1989 Peak
note: Severe GDP contraction of approximately 40% from 1989 peak confirmed. Tourism collapse and industrial decline during the war documented.

title: Washington Agreement Ends Croatian-Bosniak Conflict
note: Washington Agreement signed March 18, 1994 (not 'March 1994' exactly, but the month is correct). Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina established. Facts accurate.

title: Operation Storm Recaptures Krajina — War's Decisive Military Victory
note: Operation Storm launched August 4–7, 1995 across 630-km front. 150,000–200,000 Croatian Serbs fled. ICTY acquitted generals. Facts accurate.

title: Dayton Agreement Ends Bosnian War — Croatian Territorial Integrity Restored
note: Dayton Agreement November 1995; Erdut Agreement for Eastern Slavonia confirmed. Croatian territorial integrity restoration confirmed.

title: Croatia Joins Council of Europe
note: Croatia admitted to Council of Europe on November 6, 1996. Facts confirmed.

title: Eastern Slavonia Peacefully Reintegrated — UN Mission Succeeds
note: UNTAES mandate ended January 15, 1998; peaceful reintegration of Eastern Slavonia, Baranja and Western Sirmium confirmed. Described as one of UN's most successful peacekeeping missions.

title: President Tuđman Dies — Democratic Transition Begins
note: Tuđman died December 10, 1999. Growing authoritarianism and HDZ corruption noted by observers. Facts confirmed.

title: Democratic Transition — Opposition Wins, Mesić Elected President
note: Parliamentary elections January 3, 2000; Račan became PM January 27; Mesić won presidential runoff February 7, 2000. Croatia's EU application followed. Facts accurate.

title: General Gotovina Indicted by ICTY — National Controversy Erupts
note: Gotovina indicted by ICTY in 2001. National controversy and EU accession linkage confirmed. Facts accurate.

title: Reformed HDZ Returns to Power Under Pro-European Sanader
note: HDZ under Sanader won November 2003 elections with pro-European platform. Center-right transformation confirmed.

title: General Gotovina Arrested in Spain — EU Accession Negotiations Resume
note: Gotovina arrested December 7, 2005 in the Canary Islands (Tenerife) by Spanish police. EU accession negotiations opened October 2005. Facts accurate.

title: Zagreb-Split Motorway Completed — Croatia's Infrastructure Transformed
note: A1 motorway linking Zagreb to Split completed in mid-2000s. Infrastructure transformation and EU pre-accession funding confirmed.

title: Croatia Invited to Join NATO at Bucharest Summit
note: Croatia invited at Bucharest Summit April 2–4, 2008 alongside Albania. Became full NATO member April 1, 2009. Facts accurate.

title: Global Financial Crisis Ends Croatian Economic Boom
note: 2008 financial crisis hit Croatia's credit-fueled economy, triggering a six-year recession. GDP contraction approximately 12% from peak. Facts consistent with sources.

title: EU Accession Treaty Signed — Croatia's European Integration Milestone
note: Accession Treaty signed December 9, 2011. Referendum January 22, 2012 returned 66.3% yes. Ratification completed. Croatia joined as 28th member July 1, 2013. Facts accurate.

title: ICTY Convicts then Acquits Gotovina — Croatian Wartime Conduct Vindicated
note: Trial Chamber conviction April 15, 2011; Appeals Chamber acquittal November 16, 2012. Acquittals celebrated as vindication in Croatia. Facts accurate.

title: Croatia Joins the European Union — 28th Member State
note: Croatia joined EU on July 1, 2013 as 28th member state. Ceremony in Zagreb confirmed. ~80,000 pages of EU legislation adopted. Facts accurate.

title: Swiss Franc Mortgage Crisis — Government Orders Mandatory Loan Conversion
note: The mandatory conversion law was passed by parliament in September 2015 (following the SNB franc uncapping in January 2015), not 2014. In 2014, loans were still accumulating but no government conversion was ordered. Year off by 1 and the described action belongs to 2015.

title: Refugee Crisis — Croatia on the Balkan Migration Route
note: Croatia became major transit route in autumn 2015; hundreds of thousands crossed (over 600,000 total). Border closures and EU political controversy confirmed. Facts accurate.

title: Andrej Plenković Becomes HDZ Leader and Prime Minister
note: Plenković elected HDZ president July 2016; September 2016 elections; sworn in as PM October 19, 2016. Pro-European orientation and longevity in office confirmed.

title: Agrokor Crisis — Lex Agrokor Emergency Law Saves Croatia's Largest Company
note: Lex Agrokor passed April 6/7, 2017. Agrokor accounted for ~15-16% of GDP; total debt ~€7.8 billion. 60,000 employees confirmed. Fortenova Group outcome confirmed.

title: Croatia Reaches FIFA World Cup Final — Greatest Sporting Achievement
note: Croatia lost to France 4-2 on July 15, 2018 at Luzhniki Stadium. Modrić won Ballon d'Or 2018, ending Ronaldo-Messi duopoly. All facts confirmed.

title: Petrinja Earthquake — 6.4 Magnitude Destroys Town Center
note: Mw 6.4 earthquake struck near Petrinja on December 29, 2020. Seven killed; strongest earthquake in Croatia in over 140 years. Pandemic compounding confirmed. Facts accurate.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic Collapses Croatian Tourism Economy
note: Tourism overnight stays fell over 50% vs 2019; economy contracted ~8% in 2020. EU Council Presidency held online in H1 2020 confirmed. Facts accurate.

title: LNG Terminal at Krk Island Proves Strategic Value in Energy Crisis
note: Krk LNG terminal opened January 1, 2021 (not 2021 as stated in the source event — the event correctly notes 'opened in 2021'). Terminal's strategic value during 2022 Russian-Ukraine energy crisis confirmed. Facts accurate.

title: Croatia Joins Schengen Area and Adopts the Euro Simultaneously
note: January 1, 2023: Croatia joined Schengen (27th member) and adopted euro as 20th eurozone member. Conversion rate €1 = 7.5345 kn confirmed. Facts accurate.
